The test image shows soybean plants with severe lower leaf necrosis (tan/brown, dying leaves) while upper canopy leaves remain green. This pattern — lower leaf scorch/death with healthy upper leaves — is characteristic of Sudden Death Syndrome, Brown Stem Rot, or Phytophthora.

Let me check a Sudden Death Syndrome reference.

The SDS reference shows the classic interveinal chlorosis/necrosis pattern with green veins and yellow-brown tissue between them. The test image shows lower leaves that are entirely tan/brown and dead while upper leaves remain green — consistent with an advanced/whole-plant view of SDS where lower leaves have progressed to complete necrosis.

The field pattern (lower canopy collapse, healthy upper growth) strongly matches Sudden Death Syndrome.
